summary.tldr: Requires Canada Post to carry beer, wine and spirits across provinces to consumers, with trusted carrier exceptions and new rules for those carriers.
what_it_does: Requires Canada Post to provide postal service for interprovincial delivery of beer, wine and spirits direct to consumers.
Gives Canada Post the sole right to collect, transmit and deliver those products across provincial lines, except for trusted carriers.
Allows trusted carriers to handle interprovincial delivery of beer, wine and spirits, and lets the federal cabinet set rules for how they are chosen and monitored.
Requires the minister to publish and update a public list of trusted carriers, and lets the minister name trusted carriers before regulations are made.
Sets some changes to start three months after royal assent, and the rest to start one year after royal assent.
summary.background: Canada Post already has the exclusive privilege to collect, transmit and deliver letters, subject to exceptions. This bill adds a separate privilege and service rule for interprovincial direct-to-consumer beer, wine and spirits.
